question: Should OpenClaw solve memory-wiki isolation through a generic agents.list[].plugins override contract, a memory-wiki-specific per-agent vault contract, ctx-aware vault.path templating, or a shared/private layer model?
rationale: The choice sets security-sensitive config/API semantics for plugin state, SecretRefs, durable memory, prompt context, CLI/admin behavior, and upgrade handling; source evidence proves the gap but cannot choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
options.body: Add a shared per-agent plugin config contract with explicit precedence, schema validation, SecretRef handling, lifecycle/restart semantics, doctor/upgrade behavior, and memory-wiki coverage.

options.title: Keep plugin config global and scope memory-wiki only
options.body: Leave plugins.entries global and add memory-wiki-owned per-agent vault mapping or routing, reducing core surface but creating plugin-specific semantics.

options.title: Use ctx-aware vault path templating
options.body: Allow vault.path to expand from invocation context, but require fail-closed behavior for no-agent CLI/gateway/background surfaces and migration docs for existing shared vaults.

recommendation.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
recommendation.body: Add a shared per-agent plugin config contract with explicit precedence, schema validation, SecretRef handling, lifecycle/restart semantics, doctor/upgrade behavior, and memory-wiki coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans plugin config runtime, strict agent config schema, and security-sensitive plugin SDK behavior where recent history points most strongly to steipete.
